research.title: Exercise form does not always reveal target-muscle recruitment.
research.lead: The first design question was not how to display EMG. It was which signal could show whether the intended muscle was actually active during an exercise.
steps: Candidate A · physiological activity through surface EMG
Candidate B · angular displacement through visible contraction
Decision · select EMG after subtle contraction proved unreliable to observe geometrically
research.reverseCopy: 3-second individual calibration → filtering → squared signal → Kalman filtering → four relative-intensity bands → sample counts → session percentages.
research.note: The current result is a distribution of recorded samples across four relative EMG bands—an approximation of time distribution under stable sampling, not an automated coaching recommendation.

margin.title: No allocation method led every criterion.
margin.lead: The project compares three approaches for capacity-constrained electives.
steps: Random Ticket · randomized, less predictable outcome
Probabilistic + Maximum Weight · strongest reported satisfaction
Checked · satisfaction mean and standard deviation · completion · capacity violations
margin.reverseCopy: The final system used Simultaneous Eating for a fractional allocation, then maximum-weight realization and decomposition for concrete assignments.
margin.note: Fairness was an original project criterion, not a formally proven guarantee.

diagram.title: Residual probability needed a better rule.
diagram.lead: Some courses still had capacity while some students still had unassigned probability. Version 1 filled this gap through random course choices, which could add unnecessary probability to lower-ranked courses.
steps: Measure the capacity remaining in each course
Version 1 · select from the remaining courses at random
Failure mode · unnecessary probability on lower-ranked courses
Version 2 · balance remaining student capacity with remaining course capacity
diagram.reverseCopy: Version 2 replaced random residual assignment with a capacity-balancing rule. The goal was to reduce unnecessary low-preference allocation and produce a more even probability matrix.
diagram.note: This changed the allocation logic, not only the code.
